lessons.title: Why hides and skins have value
lessons.html:
Why hides and skins have value

A hide is the skin of a big animal, like a cow. A skin is from a small animal, like a sheep or goat. Hides and skins are sold to tanneries and made into leather for shoes, bags, car seats and jackets. Sheepskins with wool also have value. A good hide earns money for the abattoir, so careful handling matters.

What spoils a hide

  • Knife cuts and holes. These are called flay cuts. A hide with holes is worth much less.
  • Dung and dirt. They stain the hide and bring germs.
  • Heat and time. A warm hide starts to rot within hours. Hair starts to slip off.
  • Blood. Blood left on the flesh side makes the hide rot faster.
  • Folding while warm. Heat stays inside and the hide spoils.

Some damage comes from the farm, like brand marks, tick bites and thorn scratches. You cannot fix those, but you can avoid adding more damage.

Keep hides away from meat

The outside of a hide is the dirtiest part of the animal. It must never touch the meat. When the hide comes off, it goes straight down the chute or into the hide bin. Never drag a hide across the clean area of the floor.

Hides are handled in the dirty area. If you work with hides, do not walk into the clean meat area without changing your apron, washing your hands and using the boot wash. This keeps germs from the hide area away from the clean meat.

lessons.title: Salting, storing and safe handling
lessons.html:
Salting, storing and safe handling

Follow the steps used at your abattoir. A common method is:

  1. Take the hide to the hide room quickly after flaying.
  2. Spread the hide out flat, hair side down.
  3. Trim off pieces of meat, fat, ears, tail and dirty edges, as instructed.
  4. Cover the flesh side well with clean salt. Rub it in so every part is covered. Use the amount your supervisor tells you.
  5. Stack the hides flat, flesh side up, one on top of the other, with salt on each.
  6. Leave the stack to drain in a cool place with a sloping floor.
  7. Count the hides and write down the number for each day.

Some abattoirs chill hides or sell them fresh on the same day instead of salting. Then they must be kept cool and moved quickly.

Sheep and goat skins

  • Spread them flat, do not leave them in a heap.
  • Keep the wool clean and dry.
  • Salt or dry them as your abattoir instructs.

Your safety

  • A wet cattle hide is heavy. Lift with your legs, keep your back straight, and ask for help or use a hook or trolley.
  • Salt hurts cuts and eyes. Wear gloves and wash your hands after work.
  • Wear boots with a good grip. The hide room floor is wet and slippery.
  • Report any rash or sore on your skin. Hides can carry germs.

Never

  • Never fold or roll a warm hide.
  • Never leave hides in the sun.
  • Never throw hides on the meat area floor.

Key points

  • Hides and skins are sold for leather and have real value.
  • Knife holes, dirt, heat and delay spoil hides.
  • Keep hides away from the meat.
  • Spread hides flat, trim and salt them well, and stack them flesh side up.
  • Lift heavy hides safely and wear gloves.
